outcome: Project modifications (enhancing flexibility, centering cultural humility, incorporating contextual factors)
cohort: 4-6 family partners collaborated over 4 years on a multi-phase project adapting an early childhood sleep intervention for families of primarily lower socioeconomic status backgrounds, primarily Black mothers.
finding: The extensive recommended project modifications underscore the critical importance of family partnerships in promoting equity and cultural humility within pediatric psychology research and practice, further emphasizing the need for diverse representation among scholars and families.
